To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Dahl salt-sensitive rats (S), when placed on a high salt diet, have an increase in blood pressure, cardiac ouput, and peripheral resistance.
3 days high salt feeding produces hypertension in "S' rats, but not in "R" rats, and that 3 days on high salt produces vasodilation in "R" but not in "S" rat.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interrelationship of cardiac output, peripheral resistance, and arterial pressure in two strains of rats which have been bred for differences in sensitivity to NaCl hypertension.
the interrelationship of cardiac output and peripheral resistance as a possible mechanism of NaCl hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in "S" and in "R" rats, the cardiac output increases in response to 3 days of a high NaCl diet and that in "R" but not in "S" the increase in cardiac output is associated with a fall in peripheral resistance.
the concept of "autoregulation" is a useful one, but that its role in the mechanism(s) of hypertension in "S' rats is not yet known.
whole-body" regulation of cardiac output and peripheral resistance is not the sole mechanism of NaCl hypertension in the Dahl strain of rats.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mechanism of salt-induced hypertension in "R" rats is a vasodilator response to the salt, while in "S" the mechanism is a vasoconstrictor response to the salt.
NaCl-induced hypertension occurs only in rats which are genetically predisposed to hypertension.
NaCl-induced hypertension is associated with vasoconstriction and that this is a general finding in NaCl-induced hypertension, but the vasoconstriction may be due to the NaCl or to some other factor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the concept of " whole-body" autore gula tion is not applicable to all situations of hypertension.
whole-body" auto-regulation is not a causal mechanism in the genesis of NaCl hypertension in "S rats."
the peripheral vascular response to NaCl feeding in rats is not the same as the peripheral vascular response in man to NaCl feeding.
